data.hypothesis: A 32-lane X mapping makes each input-row access contiguous across a warp, while a four-output register window reuses Y neighbors and removes the baseline kernel's shared-memory/barrier path. This may improve coalescing and avoid synchronization, but trades the baseline's shared-memory reuse for rolling global loads; no speedup is assumed.
data.notes: The baseline (baseline-e1) is valid and correct, with a measured mean of 3.5815466350566667e-06 s over three reported timings. This candidate has not been oracle-checked or timed; compare only after official correctness validation and repeated full-run measurements.
transformations: Replace the shared-memory Y derivative with one kernel launch using 32 X lanes and four Y-output chunks per block-row group.
Compute four consecutive outputs per thread from a nine-value register window, shifting the window and loading one entering value between outputs.
Map each loaded Y coordinate by adding 63 below zero or subtracting 63 above 63, preserving in-range coordinate 63.
